cohort: The study included 5,670 women from the general Dutch female population, comprising nulliparous (n = 2,790) and parous (n = 2,880) individuals.
finding: The association between parity and fecal problems differs based on urinary status: nulliparous women experienced more often coexistent fecal incontinence and constipation if urinary incontinent (especially with stress urinary incontinence), and more solitary fecal incontinence if urinary continent, compared to parous women.
